solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: choices B and D are sub-intervals of C and A is the complement side of 400; a student who solves only A<C (p>400) or only A<B (p<500) still lands near C, and B/D use the irrelevant B=C crossover at 450, which is a good trap but makes the 400/500 endpoints in C stand out
minor: 2.5 F per 1,000 ft is lower than the usual atmospheric lapse rate (~3.5-5.4 F per 1,000 ft); acceptable as 'this model' but could be made more realistic (e.g., 3.5)
Q048-02.notes: Change 6,500 ft -> drop 16.25; 58-16.25=41.75. A uses 10,500 total; D adds; C uses 6,000.

Q048-03.notes: (a-3)x >= b-5; need a-3<0 and (b-5)/(a-3)=4. a=2 -> b=1. B gives x<=-4, C gives all reals, D gives x>=4 (sign trap).

Q048-04.notes: h=f-g is linear with h(0)=8, h(10)=-12; slope -2; h(x)=0 at x=4. Requires insight that the difference of linear functions is linear.

Q048-05.notes: f(x)=0.5(x+4)(x-6) from f(0)=-12. g(0)=f(-3)=0.5(1)(-9)=-4.5. C is f(3) (wrong shift direction), B is unchanged intercept.

Q048-08.notes: Mean increase (9*5+25)/10=7; median (avg of 5th and 6th, order preserved) increases 5; 7-5=2.

Q048-09.notes: 4.5 Mb/s * 7200 s = 32,400 Mb = 4,050 MB = 4.05 GB. Realistic HD streaming magnitude.

Q048-10.notes: s*sqrt2 = s+3 -> s=3(sqrt2+1)=3+3sqrt2 (choice C, the side-length trap); d=s+3=6+3sqrt2.

Q048-11.notes: Remaining sides 2*(16-8)+2*(10-8)=20; four hypotenuses 4sqrt2 -> 16sqrt2. Total 20+16sqrt2. C = rectangle perimeter.

Q048-12.notes: 64(0.5)^(t/10)=16 -> (0.5)^(t/10)=1/4 -> t/10=2 -> t=20. Realistic cooling model (86 C start, 22 C room).
